title: Residual-certified mass through preparation and clean projection
question:
Let n≥0 and let r_0,...,r_n be finite nonnegative bond dimensions with r_0=r_n=1. For j=1,...,n and t∈{0,1}, let A_j^t be a real r_{j−1} by r_j matrix. The raw vector x∈R^{2^n} has coordinates x_s=(A_1^{s_1}...A_n^{s_n})_{1,1}, with one empty word and empty product I_1 when n=0. Use Euclidean vector norms and their induced operator norms. Write T_j(Z)=Σ_{t=0}^1 A_j^t Z(A_j^t)^T and define E_n=I_1, E_{j−1}=T_j(E_j). You may use the exact Gram identity E_0(1,1)=||x||².

Suppose supplied real matrices Ē_j of size r_j by r_j satisfy Ē_n=I_1, and supplied nonnegative certificates ε_j,L_j obey
||Ē_{j−1}−T_j(Ē_j)||≤ε_j,   Σ_t||A_j^t||²≤L_j.
No positivity or canonicality of the Ē_j or the cores is assumed. Derive an explicit a posteriori number β, in terms of the ε_j,L_j, with |Ē_0(1,1)−||x||²|≤β. Give the n=0 convention. Explain why propagation factors from preceding cores cannot in general be omitted; exhibit a scalar-bond example in which replacing β by Σ_j ε_j would falsely certify positive mass for the zero raw vector.

For the remainder use your certified m:=Ē_0(1,1)−β and assume m>0. A second raw vector y∈R^{2^n} satisfies ||x−y||≤δ, where 0≤δ<√m. Prove x and y nonzero before defining ψ=x/||x|| and φ=y/||y||. You may use the supplied normalization inequality ||u/||u||−v/||v||||≤2||u−v||/||u|| for nonzero finite real or complex vectors u,v.

Let H=C^{2^n}, K=C^{2^a} with a≥0, Jv=|0^a⟩⊗v, and P=JJ†, in the fixed order K⊗H. All workspace is included in K. Two actual unitary gate lists U and V have the same length, instruction types and physical targets in every position; only Y-rotation angles differ. A rotation is R(θ)=[[cos(θ/2),−sin(θ/2)],[sin(θ/2),cos(θ/2)]], and the supplied angle error at rotation occurrence k is d_k≥0. All other gates agree exactly, including phases. Chronological products place the first gate rightmost. You may use the supplied aligned-circuit bound ||V−U||≤γ:=(1/2)Σ_k d_k. The exact preparation action is U|0^{a+n}⟩=Jφ.

For Ω=V|0^{a+n}⟩ and τ:=2δ/√m+γ, derive a full-output bound relative to Jψ. Assume τ<1 before conditioning. Decompose Ω into clean and rejected branches, prove the clean branch is nonzero, and prove that its success probability p and normalized accepted system vector ψ_acc satisfy
p≥(1−τ²/2)²,    ||ψ_acc−ψ||≤τ.
In particular justify the conditional-vector bound from the unit norm of the full output; do not silently replace it by a phase-minimized distance. Explain why τ<1 is a sufficient rather than a claimed sharp threshold, and give a unitary example with zero clean success and full-output distance √2 from a clean target.

Check zero residuals, zero data/gate errors, n=0, a=0, and an internal zero bond dimension. Keep cases that contradict m>0 separate from the active normalization theorem. State exactly which conclusions depend on the certified residuals, raw-data error, and actual circuit action/alignment; no floating-point residual certifier, angle supplier, state-loading algorithm, finite-gate-set compiler, or runtime bound is supplied.
assumptions: Finite real scalar-boundary tensor train with fixed bit order; approximate Gram environments have exact terminal I_1 and certified local operator-norm residuals ε_j and transfer bounds L_j.
For the normalization/circuit branch only: m=Ē_0(1,1)−β>0 and ||x−y||≤δ<√m with δ≥0.
The actual unitary lists are positionally aligned, differing only in same-target half-angle Y rotations with certified errors d_k; all other instructions and exact phases agree.
After φ is proved well-defined, the exact list has complete output U|0^{a+n}⟩=Jφ, including clean workspace; τ=2δ/√m+γ<1 is imposed before conditional normalization.
Exact Gram, normalization stability and aligned-circuit norm bounds are supplied interfaces; residual propagation, margin checks and downstream projection estimates are to be derived.
conventions: All vector distances compare exact representatives. Complex inner products are conjugate-linear in the first argument; real vectors embed componentwise in H.
Registers are ordered ancilla/workspace K then system H; J is the clean isometry and success projects every qubit of K onto zero.
Empty products equal 1 and empty sums 0; a zero-qubit system is one-dimensional. Zero-dimensional internal bonds are allowed and force the raw contraction to vanish.
The false-certificate example and vanishing-mass cases are diagnostics outside the active m>0 branch. No normalization of a zero vector is defined.
